Variants.Content: House Bukele is an ancient vassal of the Stormlands, with roots tied to the Bronze Gate, forest roads, and local transportation to Storm's End. The family name reflects each other's shields, passes and woodland defenses, but no heraldry can complete the vigil, bridge repair and recruitment for the lord. The middle-class families in the Stormlands often live in the gap between the great royal family and the border princes: they must be loyal to their superiors, and they must also let the people know that the castle does not exist only for distant wars.

The Stormland nobles looked at Bukele as a vassal who knew how to hold the line but could not always change the overall situation. Such a family needs to remain polite and armed among powerful neighbors. Any misjudgment may cause Tongmen to usher in enemies first.

The people of Bukele are familiar with forests, copper gates and wet roads. Soldiers hope that the castle will provide food in time, and farmers hope that patrols will stay away from their fences. The name of the lord may only be spread to neighboring counties, but the merits and demerits of guarding the bridge and protecting the harvest will be passed down locally for many generations.
Entry Buckler Entry Buckler The family crest is just a facade, the real weight of the family is whether they can protect their fiefdom, honor their engagements, and rally people in times of crisis.
Entry Buckler Entry Buckler Family reputation ultimately comes down to specific people and specific orders.

Entry Buckler Entry Buckler The ancestors of a family can be praised, or they can become a shackles for future generations; the older the bloodline, the more old debts the successors are required to bear.
Entry Buckler Entry Buckler They may not remember the complete family tree, but they remember which family opened a granary in the winter and which family drove the refugees back into the snow.
